Beamly - A Powerful Patreon Alternative with 0% Platform Fees

# Patreon vs Beamly

Beamly is a Patreon alternative for creators who want their membership to live on their own website, with control over content, branding, SEO, billing, the member experience, and how much of each sale they keep.

Patreon is a fast way to turn fans into supporters. Where it gets limiting is when the membership stops being a side project and starts becoming the business. At that point you usually need a real website, a full content library, multiple monetization paths, and predictable costs that do not scale up with every new subscriber.

That is the gap Beamly fills. It combines a creator website with memberships, paywalls, private feeds, digital products, courses, podcasts, videos, and posts. Everything can live on your own domain, and Beamly takes 0% platform fees from membership and product sales. Standard Stripe processing fees still apply.

The short answer is simple. Choose Patreon when fast setup, a familiar supporter account, and Patreon’s community tools matter most. Choose Beamly when the membership needs to become an owned podcast or creator business. For more options beyond this direct comparison, read the best Patreon alternatives.

 

## What's the difference between Beamly and Patreon?

Patreon is a well-known membership platform. It helps creators sell access to paid posts, perks, supporter tiers, and community-style updates. It is familiar to fans and easy to start.

That ease comes with tradeoffs. Patreon now supports custom domains on updated creator pages, but the experience is still Patreon-hosted and Patreon-structured. Your layout, content structure, checkout experience, and customer journey are still constrained compared with running a full website you control. Patreon also uses percentage-based platform fees, with payment processing fees on top.

Beamly gives creators the website and membership system together. You can publish free content for SEO, gate premium content for members, sell digital downloads, create online courses, offer private podcasts, and run subscriptions on your own domain. Payments and member billing live in the creator’s own Stripe account.

## Fees and revenue control

Patreon is free to start, but creators pay a percentage of successfully processed payments plus payment processing and other applicable charges.

Patreon’s standard plan charges a 10% platform fee for creator pages published after August 4, 2025. Eligible legacy pages may remain on 5%, 8%, or 11% platform fees. On the standard plan, common USD card and US PayPal or Venmo processing is 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. Currency conversion, payout, taxes on creator fees, and eligible iOS purchases may change the final amount.

Run your own prices through Beamly’s Patreon fees calculator. It explains current standard and legacy pricing, low-price examples, currency conversion, payouts, and Apple’s in-app purchase treatment.

Beamly takes 0% platform fees on subscriptions and products. Standard Stripe processing fees still apply, but Beamly does not take a percentage of membership sales.

For serious creators, this changes the math. At $5,000 in monthly member revenue, a 10% platform fee is $500 before payment processing.

As revenue grows, a percentage-based platform can take hundreds or thousands of dollars per month. Beamly’s flat plan pricing gives creators more room to invest in content, production, contractors, or member support.

## Website ownership and branding

Patreon gives creators a recognizable profile, but it is still a Patreon experience. That can be helpful for fans who already know Patreon, but it limits brand control and site architecture.

With Beamly, the membership lives on your own website. You can use your own domain, customize pages, publish SEO content, organize your library, and build trust through a site that matches your brand.

A membership is a recurring experience, not only a recurring charge. Members should be able to join, log in, browse, watch, listen, download, and learn in a place that is easy to recognize and use.

## Content and member experience

Patreon is mostly a posts-and-perks model. Updates, supporter tiers, attachments, and community-style content sit at the core of what the platform does well.

Beamly is closer to a full content hub. The same site can host public and premium blog posts, private podcasts with a unique RSS feed for each member, full YouTube libraries, premium video, courses, downloads, and gated landing pages. Each format has its own publishing structure instead of being forced into a paid post.

For podcasters, YouTubers, writers, and educators, this means fewer tools to connect. Free content for SEO, paid content for members, and products can run from one site under one brand.

### Patreon alternative for podcasters

Podcasters often need more than paid posts. They need show pages, episode pages, embeds, transcripts, SEO, private feeds, and a clean way to sell bonus content.

Beamly can host or import a public podcast, create podcast pages automatically, publish show notes and transcripts, and offer unique private podcast feeds for paid members. Patreon also supports private RSS feeds, but Beamly puts the public and private show inside a broader website with deeper page customization and SEO controls.

That distinction matters after the first few bonus episodes. Members need an archive they can browse, a clear place to manage billing, and instructions for adding a private feed to a compatible podcast app. The creator needs access rules that can cover audio, video, posts, courses, and downloads without rebuilding the offer in another tool.

### Patreon alternative for writers 

Patreon can work for paid posts and supporter updates. Beamly is stronger when a writer wants a publication website, premium archives, public SEO content, digital products, and paid membership tiers in the same place.

If your main comparison is newsletter platforms, you may also want to read Substack vs Beamly and Ghost vs Beamly.

### Patreon alternative for course creators 

Patreon is not built as a course platform. Beamly can support courses, lessons, premium videos, downloads, and membership access rules. That makes it easier to sell education content as a subscription, bundle, or one-time product.

### Patreon alternative for digital product sellers 

Patreon can sell one-time products and perks, but it is not built as a full digital product storefront. Beamly includes digital downloads and an online store, so creators can sell templates, guides, files, and bundles alongside memberships.

## Patreon vs Beamly feature comparison

With no transaction fees and a full website building platform, there's no debate - Beamly is the best Patreon alternative and the only platform you'll need for your membership website.

###### Can Beamly replace Patreon? 

Yes. Beamly can replace Patreon for creators who want memberships, paid content, private feeds, products, and subscriptions on their own website.

###### Can I offer private podcast feeds on Beamly? 

Yes. Beamly supports private podcasts and unique member feeds, which makes it a strong Patreon alternative for podcasters.

###### Do I need a separate website if I use Beamly? 

No. Beamly includes a website builder, publishing tools, memberships, products, courses, podcast features, and SEO tools.

###### Can I sell free and paid memberships? 

Yes. Beamly supports free and paid membership tiers, so you can collect free members and offer paid upgrades.
